UI fixes, slice A: the model

DFMA Review · 2026-11-11 · draft PR #51 (not merged) · spec docs/specs/ui-fixes.md S1

Slice A is built and every check passes. The part now turns freely, like Inventor's free orbit. Five view buttons put it back. A small XYZ in the corner shows the part's own axes. Pins hide while the part moves. Picking a row lights one feature, and the rest of the part goes grey.

Try it: the demo, or the work copy once this merges. Tap report_sample, then Features. Open "Deep hole ×2": one hole lights, and › lights the other. Drag to spin the part and watch the pins go and come back. Press each view button.

To decide

1. Approve PR #51 to merge, or tell me what to change. Slice B (examples, Open…, the machine view) starts in a new session once it merges.

2. Drag speed on big parts. The spec's goal was a frame every 50 ms or less while turning CTC 02. Here it is about 190 ms, down from 310-420 ms. The page itself now does almost no work while you drag: 0.2 s against 11-15 s before. What's left looks like this container drawing in software. Your PC's graphics card should be much faster. Please tell me how it feels at work.

3. Arrow keys. I made each arrow move the camera that way: ← goes round to the left, so the part seems to turn right. If you'd rather the part follows the arrow, it's a one-line change.

Screens (tap to zoom)

Calls I made while building

  • three's free-orbit control had two bugs in the way we use it: the first pan or zoom jumped by about the part's size, and it lost track of which way is up. I added a two-line fix for each, and the tests cover both.
  • A row now lights the finding it shows, so six older checks expected the whole row. I changed them to the new behaviour; none got weaker.
  • The triad sits 24 px up so its caption fits under it (the spec's numbers made them overlap).
  • A fresh reviewer read the code against the spec and found 8 items. All are fixed: pins could stay hidden after a cancelled touch, and 3 checks couldn't fail.

Checks

  • npm run check: 838 unit tests, parity 122 of 122, 108 browser tests and 69 timed tests passed, in 662 s (budget 900 s).
  • The 9 new browser tests each failed on main first. Planted bugs (pins back at 0 ms, colours kept while selected, a wrong Top view, the triad in the PDF) each made their test fail.
  • The demo can't save a PDF inside the page viewer, the same as earlier demos.
